front_question: Define gene, allele, genotype, phenotype, dominant trait, and recessive trait.
back_answer: Gene: Functional unit of DNA coding for a specific protein/trait. Allele: Alternative form of a gene (e.g. T or t). Genotype: Genetic makeup of an organism (e.g. TT, Tt, tt). Phenotype: Observable physical trait (e.g. Tall, Dwarf). Dominant Trait: Trait expressed in heterozygous state (Tt = Tall). Recessive Trait: Trait expressed only in homozygous state (tt = Dwarf).

front_question: State the phenotypic and genotypic ratios obtained in the F2 generation of a Mendelian Monohybrid Cross.
back_answer: Crossing pure Tall (TT) and Dwarf (tt) pea plants gives F1 all Tall (Tt). F2 selfing (Tt x Tt) yields: Phenotypic Ratio = 3 Tall : 1 Dwarf (3:1). Genotypic Ratio = 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt (1:2:1).

front_question: What phenotypic ratio is obtained in a Mendelian Dihybrid Cross, and what law does it demonstrate?
back_answer: Crossing pure Round Yellow (RRYY) and Wrinkled Green (rryy) pea plants gives F1 all Round Yellow (RrYy). F2 selfing yields phenotypic ratio = 9 Round Yellow : 3 Round Green : 3 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green (9:3:3:1). This demonstrates Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.

front_question: Explain chromosomal sex determination in humans with a genetic cross diagram description.
back_answer: Human body cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes (22 autosome pairs + 1 sex chromosome pair). Females are XX (produce all X eggs); Males are XY (produce 50% X sperms and 50% Y sperms). Genetic Cross: Mother (XX) x Father (XY) -> 50% chance XX (Female child) and 50% chance XY (Male child). Hence, the father's sperm type determines the sex of the child.
